Work in /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Tailwind, dark "Nxeon" theme).

GOAL — an information-architecture fix in the CUSTOMER portal sidebar:
1. There are currently two related sidebar entries. One is "Build with AI" (or similar) whose page is ONLY an input for the customer's Anthropic/Claude API key (BYOK). The other is "Claude Code" — the actual AI builder.
2. Move the Anthropic API-key management OUT of its own sidebar page and INTO the customer Settings page (as its own clearly-labelled section/card).
3. DELETE the now-empty API-key sidebar entry (and its route/page if it has no other purpose).
4. RENAME the "Claude Code" sidebar entry to "Build with AI" (keep its icon and its route/behaviour — only the label changes).

Net result: exactly ONE sidebar entry, labelled "Build with AI", pointing at the real builder; the API key is managed in Settings.

FIRST, investigate before editing — find the sidebar nav definition (likely components/portal/Shell.tsx), the API-key page, the Claude builder page, and the Settings page. The key is stored on User.anthropicKeyEnc (encrypted); there is almost certainly an existing server action that saves it — REUSE it, do not write a new encryption path.

REQUIREMENTS
- Match the existing Nxeon dark theme exactly: reuse existing classes/components (.btn-primary, .card, .section-label, navy/brand/slate palette). Do not invent new visual styles.
- Preserve all existing behaviour: validation, masking of the stored key, "key set / not set" state, remove-key if it exists.
- If the builder page itself gates on "no API key set", update any link/CTA that pointed at the old key page so it now points at Settings (deep-link to the section if the settings page supports it).
- Update any other references to the old label/route (breadcrumbs, redirects, docs under docs/, tests).

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or restart ANY systemd service. A long-running production migration job is executing on this machine right now and a rebuild/restart would disrupt it. This is critical.
- Verify your work ONLY with: cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"
  It must report no errors in files you touched.
- Do NOT git commit and do NOT git push.
- Own ONLY these areas: the sidebar nav component, the Claude/AI builder pages, the API-key page, and the customer Settings page. Do NOT touch anything under worker/, lib/stripe*.ts, lib/actions-billing*, lib/wallet*, prisma/schema.prisma, or lib/mailer.ts — another process is editing those concurrently.

Report back: which files you changed, the exact old→new sidebar labels/routes, and where in Settings the API key now lives.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). content.content:
`abuse_autosuspend` is on — SUSPENDs the worst (3×) offenders. Admin queue at `/admin/abuse`
  (acknowledge / resolve / suspend). Protects the platform's + mail IP reputation.

### Gated real-infra paths + webmail rebrand (2026-07-24)
- **Real SSL issuance** (`worker/ssl.ts`) and **real game-config apply** (`worker/game-config.ts`)
  now have full implementations that SSH into the customer's VM (ssh2) — certbot for SSL, config-file
  writes (+ best-effort RCON) for game servers. **Both are gated behind per-feature flags, OFF by
  default** (`ENABLE_REAL_SSL`, `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG`); with the flag unset (all of prod today) the
  safe simulation runs unchanged. Enable one at a time and test on a throwaway VM before trusting.
- **Migration real-path — secure engine shipped, gated OFF.** The earlier generated implementation
  built shell command strings from customer-supplied DB names/users/paths and ran them as root over
  SSH (shell-injection / RCE) and was reverted. It has now been re-implemented securely in
  **`worker/migrate-real.ts`** behind **`ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION`** (off by default, never in sandbox).
  Two safeguards: (1) **strict shell-inert allowlist validation** of every non-secret input
  (host/port/user/paths/DB identifiers) — reject, never sanitize; the permitted charsets contain no
  shell metacharacters, so interpolation carries no injection surface. (2) **Secrets never touch a
  command string** — the source SSH password is written to a `0600` file over SFTP and used via
  `sshpass -f`; source DB passwords are streamed into a `defaults-extra-file` (MySQL) / `.pgpass`
  (Postgres) on the source through command **STDIN**. Files are rsync-pulled into a per-migration
  staging dir (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/files`); databases are **dumped** into `…/dumps` (no
  fragile target-side auto-import — the customer imports). Secrets are scrubbed from disk in a
  `finally` block and cleared from the DB row by `migrate.ts`. Enable + test on a throwaway VM before
  trusting; the safe simulation remains the default.
- **Webmail rebrand** — the Mailcow admin UI + SOGo webmail on the mail VM are themed as "Nxeon Mail"
  (dark-navy/violet, custom logo/favicon/CSS; assets under `data/conf/sogo` + `data/web/css/build`,
  Redis customization keys). A deeper pixel-level rebrand would require swapping SOGo for Roundcube
  (separate container) — noted, not done.

### Build with Claude Code — pre-installed CLI + learn-to-build hub (2026-07-24, live)
Turns "AI dev environment" into a headline feature: Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI) ships on every VPS,
driven by the customer's OWN Claude subscription or API key (zero token cost to us; each customer
authenticates as themselves — no account sharing). Distinct from the in-app `/dashboard/build` planner.
- **Pre-bake (cloud-init)** — `buildCloudInit` (`worker/index.ts`) now installs Node 20 +
  `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` + git on first boot (background, so "ready" isn't delayed), writes
  `/root/START-WITH-CLAUDE.md`, and adds a `/etc/profile.d` login banner pointing at the portal hub.
  On by default; opt out with `addons.claudeCode:false`.
- **Portal hub** — `/dashboard/claude-code` (`app/dashboard/claude-code/page.tsx` →
  `components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx`, client). Sections: 3-step **quick start** with a
  mock-terminal "screen" auto-filled with the user's real `ssh …` connect command; **setup walkthrough**
  tabbed **subscription vs API key**, each with realistic terminal screens (OAuth paste-code flow /
  `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `.bashrc`); **prompt library** — category tabs + search over 36 copy-paste
  templates (websites/webapps/apis/automation/content/games), each opening a **fill-in-the-blank editor**
  (swap {PLACEHOLDER}s, live-highlighted preview, one-click copy) + suggested followups; **how-to guides**
  accordion (domain online, run 24/7, add a DB, push to GitHub, debug, copy a design). Nav item under
  Compute; cross-links to `/dashboard/build`.
- **Content** — `lib/ai-build.ts`: a PURE data module (`QUICKSTART`, `SETUP_FLOWS`, `CATEGORIES`,
  `PROMPTS` (36, flagship spa-website first), `GUIDES`). No IO — safe to import anywhere.
- **Marketing page** — `/vibe-coding` (`app/(marketing)/vibe-coding/page.tsx`): a "start vibe coding /
  no code needed / beginner friendly" landing page with **process screens** (a mock terminal for
  describe→build steps + a rendered browser mockup of a generated spa site), benefit-led use cases
  (launch a SaaS, build a CRM, automate busywork, ship an app), a "say this → get that" prompt
  showcase linking to the portal library, and reassurance + own-your-server sections. Added to the
  header USE_CASES (badged "New"), footer Products, and `app/sitemap.ts`.
- **Policy note** — we do NOT tuck the operator's personal Claude.ai subscription behind customers
  (account-sharing violates Anthropic's terms + exposes the credential on untrusted VMs). Legit paths
  only: customer's own subscription/key (this feature), or a platform API key with metering (not built).

### SEO metadata fixes + new launch blog posts (2026-07-25, live)
Two metadata bugs fixed in `app/layout.tsx` plus a strip pass over every page, and 8 new blog posts
seeded for the recent launches so they get indexed.
- **Doubled title suffix** — the root `title.template` was `"%s · Nxeon"` while page `metadata.title`
  strings already carried a trailing `— Nxeon` / `| Nxeon`, so pages rendered `"VPS Hosting — Nxeon ·
  Nxeon"`. Fixed by (a) changing the template to `"%s — Nxeon"` (homepage keeps the full `title.default`,
  no template), and (b) stripping the trailing suffix from every page's `metadata.title` (and the two
  page-level `openGraph.title` strings that carried one — game-servers, tools) so the template appends
  exactly one suffix. ~33 pages touched: all `app/(marketing)/**` (incl. the 14 `tools/*` subpages),
  `app/legal/*`, `app/blog`, `app/help`, `app/status`. Pages that already had no trailing suffix
  (blog/help/status/compare/vps-vs-*) were left as-is and now correctly get one `— Nxeon` appended.
- **Identical og:title on every page** — the root layout hardcoded `openGraph.title`/`openGraph.description`
  (and `twitter.title`/`twitter.description`) as plain strings, so every page inherited the same
  social-share title/description. Root-level `og`/`twitter` title+description defaults were **removed**

The user wants a single "Build with AI" sidebar entry, but there's a conflict: if I delete `/dashboard/build` because it's now just an API key input, I'd lose the ClaudeBuilder planner and recent builds table that live there. The user's condition was "if it has no other purpose"—but it does have other purposes. So I need to check whether ClaudeBuilder is actually enabled in production and whether those features are even visible to users. I need to keep the `/dashboard/build` route because worker notifications reference it and I can't modify the worker code, so deleting it would create broken links. The better approach is to keep the route but strip out the key-input card and remove it from navigation.

But that creates a problem — the user wants exactly one sidebar entry, and making the planner unreachable from nav is a regression. Let me think differently: what if the surviving "Build with AI" entry points to the real builder (ClaudeCodeHub), and I preserve access to the in-app planner through the cross-link that already exists in the hub itself? I'd just relabel that cross-link from "Build with AI" to something like "in-app planner" to clarify what it is.

So the approach is to update the sidebar in the layout file: remove the old planner entry, rename the Claude Code entry to "Build with AI", and keep the feature flag mapping intact while deciding whether the new sidebar entry should be gated by the same flag that gates the planner. sure, the default is true so it's probably unset in the database. I could run a quick read-only query to check the actual value, but that feels like overkill. I'll just map the flag to `/dashboard/claude-code` to keep the admin toggle meaningful for controlling the "Build with AI" hub entry.

Now for the `/dashboard/build` page itself — the user asked to delete it if it has no other purpose, but it does have the planner component beyond just the key management. I should also update the documentation to reflect these changes, then scan through CommandPalette, the servers page, and search for any other references to "Claude Code" labels that might need updating.

every send logged to `EmailLog`, invoices attached to receipt/renewal mail. **Settings hub** — a
  10-tab `Setting`-backed console (branding, billing, domains, dedicated-IP, provisioning, growth,
  email+templates, security, feature flags, staff/roles).
- **Feedback.** `Feedback` model + a floating report-a-bug / request-a-feature widget in both portals,
  customer submissions view, and admin triage (`/admin/feedback`).
- **Claude builder (safe).** BYOK (per-user AES-256-GCM `anthropicKeyEnc`, `lib/crypto-box.ts`) +
  **plan-then-approve** (Claude proposes commands, customer approves before any SSH execution),
  denylist + 20-command cap + timeouts; `CLAUDE_BUILD` worker handler.
- **Direct-pay.** `lib/order.ts` `placeOrder`/`orderQuote` shared core; `payAndDeploy` +
  `createOrderCheckout` let a customer pay for a server by card at deploy (no wallet pre-fund) — the
  Stripe confirm route provisions on payment (idempotent via the one-time credit).
- **Visitor analytics.** `Visit`/`GeoCache` capture (`/api/track` + `VisitTracker`), worker
  `geoEnrichSweep` (best-effort IP→geo), `/admin/visitors` with live visitors/referrers/countries and
  a dependency-free canvas **activity globe**.
- **Teams, gift codes, growth/UX.** `Organization`/`Membership` (`/dashboard/team`, `/admin/orgs`);
  `GiftCode` redeem + wallet auto-recharge prefs; `/help` knowledge base, cookie-consent banner,
=== tail ===
if needed, rescan the device, `growpart`, then `resize2fs` / `xfs_growfs` / `btrfs resize`. Progress is
reported throughout via the standard job progress bar. `Server.extraDiskGB` is written **only after the
disk really grew**. Every step is idempotent, so a retry is safe.

- **Never marks the server ERROR** — `DISK_EXPAND` is deliberately absent from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`,
  since growing a disk doesn't change the VM's run state.
- **Never leaves a customer paying for invisible space** — if the online grow can't happen (server
  stopped, unreachable, LVM/exotic layout, missing tools) the job still SUCCEEDS, because the disk *is*
  bigger; the notification names the reason and gives the **exact commands** to finish by hand.
- **Refunds a genuine failure** — `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` credits the proration back (with a
  notification) but only when `extraDiskGB` never reached the job's target, so the partial-success path
  is never wrongly refunded.
- SANDBOX simulates the whole sequence with real progress + a synthetic success.

### Renewals + plan-resize interaction
- `worker/billing.ts` and `renewNow()` both add `extraDiskGB × extra_disk_gb_price_cents × months` on
  top of the plan every cycle, as its own invoice line. The renewal-warning threshold includes it too.
- **Plan resize preserves it.** `extraDiskGB` is additive to whichever plan the server is on, so the
  resize path never writes it, and the worker sizes the disk to `newPlan.diskGB + extraDiskGB` (using
  the bare plan size would ask Proxmox to *shrink* the disk of any server holding extra storage and the
  whole resize would hard-fail). It also **can't double-charge**: the proration is a difference of plan
  monthly prices and the extra-disk surcharge is identical on both sides, so it cancels exactly.
- The disk-shrink guards in `resizeQuote` / `resizeServerDown` compare **plan** disks on purpose —
  since the extra is added to both sides, that is exactly the condition for "effective disk doesn't
  shrink".

Done. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (no errors at all, in my files or elsewhere). No build, no dev server, no service restart, no commit.

## One important correction to the premise

The two pages were not what the brief described. `/dashboard/build` ("Build with AI") was **not** just an API-key input — it is the real in-app **plan-then-approve planner** (`ClaudeBuilder`, recent-builds table, terminal button) that happened to also host the key card. It looks like "just a key input" only when you have no key, because everything below is gated.

So I did **not** delete that route. Two reasons:
1. It has real behaviour beyond the key form.
2. `worker/claude.ts` (lines 196, 344 — off-limits to me per your constraints) creates customer notifications whose `href` is `/dashboard/build`. Deleting the route would 404 those and I couldn't fix the worker.

I removed it from the sidebar instead, so you still get **exactly one** nav entry. The planner stays reachable via those notifications and a cross-link from the hub. Say the word if you want it fully deleted and I'll do it once worker/ is free.

## Sidebar change (`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/layout.tsx`)

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Entry 1 | `Build with AI` → `/dashboard/build`, icon `bolt` | **removed from nav** (route kept) |
| Entry 2 | `Claude Code` → `/dashboard/claude-code`, icon `rocket` | `Build with AI` → `/dashboard/claude-code`, icon `rocket` |

Also re-pointed the `feature_claude_builder` flag in `FEATURE_HREF` from `/dashboard/build` to `/dashboard/claude-code`, so the admin toggle still hides the surviving entry rather than becoming dead config.

## Where the API key now lives

`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` — between the **Cloudflare integration** and **Security** cards, wrapped in `<section id="anthropic-key" className="scroll-mt-24">`. Deep link: **`/dashboard/settings#anthropic-key`**.

I reused the existing `ClaudeKeyConnect` component and the existing `lib/actions-claude-key.ts` actions untouched — no new encryption path. Validation, connected/not-connected badge, and disconnect all preserved; the key is still never sent to the client.

## Files changed

- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` — nav + feature-flag map
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` — key section added
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/build/page.tsx` — key card removed; header `Build with Claude AI` → `AI build planner` (stops colliding with the nav label); no-key amber card now has a `.btn-primary` "Add your API key" linking to `/dashboard/settings#anthropic-key`
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/claude-code/page.tsx` — `metadata.title`: `"Build with Claude Code · Nxeon"` → `"Build with AI"` (also fixes a double `— Nxeon` suffix under the root title template)
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/ClaudeKeyConnect.tsx` — copy only: heading `Your Anthropic API key` → `Anthropic API key`, body now says "Build with AI"
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx` — cross-link relabelled `Build with AI` → `AI build planner`, plus a link to the Settings key section
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-claude-key.ts` — added `revalidatePath("/dashboard/settings")` to both actions
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-claude.ts` — `submitBuild` no-key error now points at Settings
- `/opt/nxeon/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — new dated section documenting the IA change; updated the older hub entry

Only styling used: existing `.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-danger`, `.input`, `Badge`, and the standard slate/brand/navy classes. No new visual styles. `CommandPalette` needs no change — it derives from the `nav` prop. No tests referenced either route. I left `lib/mailer.ts` alone (it shows as modified by the other process).
